A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProNC research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments on Seq-CIFAR-10, Seq-CIFAR-100, and Seq-TinyImageNet, including accuracy, forgetting, ablations, feature analyses, and training times.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical studies and reports additional baseline comparisons, ETF-size experiments, and integrations of ProNC into other learning methods.

M1.justification: The core ETF initialization, expansion, losses, and inference rule remain unchanged. A limited procedural extension appears in Section 4.3: the DER++ integration retains the baseline's original components while adding alignment and feature-wise distillation, beyond v1's documented alignment-only integrations into iCaRL and LUCIR.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three image datasets under Class-IL and Task-IL. Empty-buffer evaluation already appears in v1. The added ETF-size and method-integration experiments change configurations and comparisons within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds LODE, STAR, and CSReL to Table 1. Its empty-buffer Table 2 adds Co2L and MNC3L comparators to a setting where v1 reported only ProNC results. The generality comparison also expands from iCaRL/LUCIR to ER, DER++, XDER, and STAR/LODE-enhanced alternatives.

E3.justification: The existing dataset partitions, modified ResNet-18, batch size, training epochs, memory budgets, metrics, and ProNC hyperparameter grids are retained. v2 adds an NCT experiment varying the predefined ETF size, including K=1000, and specifies using ER+STAR for the main STAR comparison.

E4.justification: New Figure 1 directly tests sensitivity to overprovisioning NCT's fixed ETF. The generality analysis expands substantially to additional host methods and competing regularizers, and empty-buffer performance gains matched baseline controls. The component, feature-correlation, hyperparameter, and alternative-loss studies already existed; the loss-flexibility study is relocated from v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report multiple-run averages and appendix results with plus/minus uncertainty values, without specifying run counts, seeds, or confidence-interval procedures. Additional baseline rows follow the existing reporting practice; no new statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, ETF-size, integration, and empty-buffer comparison results. Core ProNC Table 1 scores remain unchanged, but ER's buffer-500 CIFAR-100 Class-IL accuracy changes from 27.66 to 22.35, and ProNC's empty-buffer CIFAR-100 Class-IL/Task-IL accuracies change from 30.87/84.33 to 32.28/84.62. New LODE results exceed ProNC on CIFAR-10 Class-IL. The stated TinyImageNet margin changes from 111.40% to 59.32%, although v2 Table 1's 27.44 versus 18.14 implies approximately 51.27%.

T1.justification: The ETF definition, neural-collapse properties, nearest-ETF theorem, SVD lemma, and proof are substantively unchanged. The proof moves from Appendix B to Appendix D. Equation renumbering and the numerical illustration of the existing ETF inner-product formula add no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: progressive ETF construction without advance knowledge of the total class count, a simple alignment-and-distillation framework, and strong accuracy, efficiency, flexibility, and forgetting performance. Expanded experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds an applicability argument that STAR and LODE require separate treatment of current and replay data, making them unsuitable for the discussed iCaRL/LUCIR integrations. It removes v1's explanation attributing GSS's latency to quadratic gradient-correlation computations. The clear-task-boundary limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link in the abstract and a reproducibility statement directing readers to implementation details and supplementary code. v1 already disclosed Mammoth-based supplementary code, hardware, backbone modifications, batch size, hyperparameters, and search grids; these details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds STAR, CSReL, and LODE references and directly discusses NCT's proposed use of a larger predefined ETF. It removes the pretrained-model related-work category and its five associated references. The central positioning against fixed-ETF continual learning remains unchanged; publication updates for existing citations are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: Related Work moves to Appendix A, generality and loss-flexibility discussions move into the main experiments, and training-cost discussion moves to Appendix C.3. Appendices are reorganized, prose is locally condensed, and reproducibility, ethics, acknowledgements, and LLM-usage statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds an ETF-size bar chart and an empty-buffer comparison table, expands several comparison tables, and relocates generality, loss-design, and timing tables across the main text and appendices. Conference typography, headers, and table formatting replace the preprint layout. The original workflow diagram and six-panel analysis figure are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, ETF-size analysis, broader integration tests, and code link improve validation and accessibility. However, new evidence introduces material inconsistencies: STAR's buffer-200 CIFAR-100 Class-IL accuracy is 38.15 in Table 1 but 18.29 in Appendix Table 9. The retained claim of outperforming every baseline also conflicts with LODE's CIFAR-10 accuracy of 68.01 versus ProNC's 65.58. These problems undermine the added comparisons, leaving the net effect of broader evidence and weaker internal consistency uncertain.
